_meta.description: Field-experiment and inter-review-agreement figures used by the study (handoff §10.1, §10.2). Each item has value, source, handoff status and the result of the 2026-10-02 check. Derived values are computed from the raw counts.

status_key.V: verified by the author against the primary source on 2 Oct 2026
status_key.P: read from a primary page or paper but not re-verified

neurips2014.description: NeurIPS 2014: about 10% of submissions were reviewed by two independent committees.

design.note: 170 papers (about 10% of 1,678) were chosen; 4 were withdrawn or rejected without review, so 166 have two decisions.
design.source: Cortes & Lawrence, 'Inconsistency in Conference Peer Review: Revisiting the 2014 NeurIPS Experiment', arXiv:2109.09774

table_2x2.orientation: Cortes & Lawrence Table 1: rows committee 2, columns committee 1. The handoff's '22 accepted by committee A only' is committee 2 only; '21 by committee B only' is committee 1 only.
table_2x2.source: Cortes & Lawrence, 'Inconsistency in Conference Peer Review: Revisiting the 2014 NeurIPS Experiment', arXiv:2109.09774; Lawrence, 'The NIPS experiment', inverseprobability.com, 16 Dec 2014

check.note: Lawrence's 2014 blog gives only 25.9%; the table is in the 2021 paper.

derived.note: Computed from table_2x2. The handoff's '50 percent and 51 percent rejected by the other' is wrong for the second share: 21/43 = 49% were rejected; 51% is the share the other committee accepted. Section 2.2 of the paper has the typo '25.0%' for 25.9%.
derived.source: Cortes & Lawrence, 'Inconsistency in Conference Peer Review: Revisiting the 2014 NeurIPS Experiment', arXiv:2109.09774

quoted_57_percent.note: E. Price applied the 22.5% rate that the committees were 'tasked with' (37 or 38 accepts of 166) to the 43 inconsistent papers: 21/37 or 22/38, about 57%. 22.5% was a target rate, not the realised conference-wide rate (24.7%). Cortes & Lawrence Appendix C.1 agrees that the debate used the main conference rate as a proxy.
quoted_57_percent.source: Price, guest post on Moritz Hardt's blog, 15 Dec 2014; Cortes & Lawrence, 'Inconsistency in Conference Peer Review: Revisiting the 2014 NeurIPS Experiment', arXiv:2109.09774 Appendix C.1

check.note: Confirmed with one change: 22.5% was the target rate, not the realised rate.

committee_score_correlation.note: Correlation of the two committees' mean calibrated scores (paper Fig. 2). The handoff's notebook value 0.544 is the raw (uncalibrated) correlation; the calibrated notebook value is 0.5456. In the model this maps to rho^2 directly (r12 = rho^2).
committee_score_correlation.source: Cortes & Lawrence, 'Inconsistency in Conference Peer Review: Revisiting the 2014 NeurIPS Experiment', arXiv:2109.09774; Lawrence, slides 16 Jun 2021; lawrennd/neurips2014 'Reviewer Calibration' notebook

variance_components.note: Fitted variance components of individual review scores (paper Table 2). Units: squared points on the 2014 1-10 scale.
variance_components.source: Cortes & Lawrence, 'Inconsistency in Conference Peer Review: Revisiting the 2014 NeurIPS Experiment', arXiv:2109.09774 Table 2; Lawrence, slides 16 Jun 2021

check.note: Table 2; the same values are on Lawrence's 2021 slides.

score_citation_correlation.note: Correlation between review scores and later citations. Not significant among accepted papers.
score_citation_correlation.source: Cortes & Lawrence, 'Inconsistency in Conference Peer Review: Revisiting the 2014 NeurIPS Experiment', arXiv:2109.09774 Figs. 4 and 8

neurips2021.description: NeurIPS 2021: 10% of papers were duplicated at assignment and reviewed by two independent committees (separate ACs, SACs and reviewers).

design.note: 882 duplicated papers were still under review when initial reviews were released. 118 were withdrawn by the authors after initial reviews; they appear as withdrawn in both copies and so agree by construction. Each copy had its own AC and SAC; the same four PCs worked on both copies (an inference, not stated in the paper). A duplicated paper was accepted if either copy was recommended for acceptance. Duplicated papers had a lower acceptance rate (22.7%) than other papers under review (2,036/7,883 = 25.8%).
design.source: Beygelzimer, Dauphin, Liang & Wortman Vaughan, 'Has the Machine Learning Review Process Become More Arbitrary as the Field Has Grown? The NeurIPS 2021 Consistency Experiment', arXiv:2306.03262 Sections 2-3

table1.note: Recommendations after SAC/PC calibration. Rows: original committee; columns: copy committee. Orientation checked from the rendered PDF (row accepts 206, column accepts 195).
table1.source: Beygelzimer, Dauphin, Liang & Wortman Vaughan, 'Has the Machine Learning Review Process Become More Arbitrary as the Field Has Grown? The NeurIPS 2021 Consistency Experiment', arXiv:2306.03262 Table 1; NeurIPS blog 8 Dec 2021 (same table as an image)

accept_level.note: The quoted '203 (23.0%) inconsistent at 22.7% average acceptance; random 35.1%' uses all 882 papers and counts the 118 withdrawn papers as consistent rejects. The decided_764 basis drops them. src/peerreview/calibrate.py uses decided_764 as the central calibration target (NEURIPS2021) and keeps all_882 as NEURIPS2021_ALL.
accept_level.source: Beygelzimer, Dauphin, Liang & Wortman Vaughan, 'Has the Machine Learning Review Process Become More Arbitrary as the Field Has Grown? The NeurIPS 2021 Consistency Experiment', arXiv:2306.03262 Section 4.1; NeurIPS blog 8 Dec 2021

check.note: 206 and 195 accepts, 99 in both; recomputed from Table 1.

oral_only.note: All 6 orals were posters in the other copy.

top_tier.pairing: 13 of 29 and 13 of 25 are the oral+spotlight tiers. 13 of 25 and 13 of 23 are the spotlight-only tiers. The two '13 of 25' figures come from different committees. The handoff §8.1 reconstruction pairs the spotlight rejection counts with the oral+spotlight sizes; scripts/run_validation_neurips2021.py uses the correct pairing.
top_tier.note: The paper text gives 5.8% disagreement if only orals and spotlights were accepted, but Table 1 gives 48/882 = 5.4%. The paper's '8% relative improvement' over the 5.9% random baseline fits 5.4%; the blog says 3%.
top_tier.source: Beygelzimer, Dauphin, Liang & Wortman Vaughan, 'Has the Machine Learning Review Process Become More Arbitrary as the Field Has Grown? The NeurIPS 2021 Consistency Experiment', arXiv:2306.03262 Table 1 and Section 4.1; NeurIPS blog 8 Dec 2021 (spotlight counts)

check.note: The blog states 13/25 and 13/23 for spotlights; the paper gives only Table 1.

committee_score_correlation.note: The handoff (§10.1, §10.7) says this was not reported. It is reported in the caption of Figure 1. In the model it maps to rho^2 directly (r12 = rho^2). calibrate.py already uses it (NEURIPS2021_SCORE_CORR).
committee_score_correlation.source: Beygelzimer, Dauphin, Liang & Wortman Vaughan, 'Has the Machine Learning Review Process Become More Arbitrary as the Field Has Grown? The NeurIPS 2021 Consistency Experiment', arXiv:2306.03262 Figure 1 caption

disagreement_by_score_threshold.note: No table by score band. Figures 2 and 3 plot the disagreement and the rejected-by-other share against the acceptance rate if the top x% by mean initial or final score were accepted. The curves are available only as figures.
disagreement_by_score_threshold.source: Beygelzimer, Dauphin, Liang & Wortman Vaughan, 'Has the Machine Learning Review Process Become More Arbitrary as the Field Has Grown? The NeurIPS 2021 Consistency Experiment', arXiv:2306.03262 Figures 2 and 3

check.note: Threshold curves exist as figures only.

variants.note: Variants that apply the AC's 'can be bumped up/down' qualifiers. Not a handoff claim.
variants.source: Beygelzimer, Dauphin, Liang & Wortman Vaughan, 'Has the Machine Learning Review Process Become More Arbitrary as the Field Has Grown? The NeurIPS 2021 Consistency Experiment', arXiv:2306.03262

check.note: Read from the paper by the NeurIPS verifier.

recommendation_process.value: The AC meta-review form had a mandatory field: Accept (Oral), Accept (Spotlight), Accept (Poster) or Reject, with a qualifier (certain; can be bumped up; can be bumped down; not certain). SACs and PCs decided orals and spotlights jointly, using factors beyond raw scores. During calibration ACs were often asked to edit meta-reviews between poster and reject or between spotlight and poster.
recommendation_process.source: Beygelzimer, Dauphin, Liang & Wortman Vaughan, 'Has the Machine Learning Review Process Become More Arbitrary as the Field Has Grown? The NeurIPS 2021 Consistency Experiment', arXiv:2306.03262 Sections 2, 4.2, 5.1 and Appendix B

conference_totals.note: The handoff gives 25.7%; the fact sheet and the paper give 25.6%.
conference_totals.source: NeurIPS 2021 fact sheet; Beygelzimer, Dauphin, Liang & Wortman Vaughan, 'Has the Machine Learning Review Process Become More Arbitrary as the Field Has Grown? The NeurIPS 2021 Consistency Experiment', arXiv:2306.03262 Section 2

iclr_review_agreement.description: Agreement between individual ICLR reviews of the same paper (OpenReview data).

berenslab_review_correlation.note: 244,226 counts ordered pairs, so each pair is counted twice. The figure pools three rating scales (1-10; 1/3/6/8 in 2020; 1/3/5/6/8/10 from 2022).
berenslab_review_correlation.source: berenslab ICLR dataset README (version 24v2 statistics) and arXiv:2404.08403

check.note: Verifier recompute from the paperlists dumps: r = 0.399 over 244,234 ordered pairs (122,117 distinct), 3.66 reviews per reviewed paper, 92.8% with 3 or 4.

recompute_in_repo.note: Values as of 2026-10-02; rerun scripts/iclr_data.py to refresh.

icc1_by_year.note: Own one-way ICC(1) of individual scores from the paperlists dumps. Verifier recompute: 0.576, 0.413, 0.464, 0.392. The handoff's SD ranges (within 1.03-1.19, between 1.00-1.20) hold for 2017-2019 only; 2020 (1/3/6/8 scale) has within SD 1.72 and between SD 1.38. ICC(1) is 0.36-0.42 for 2021-2025 and 0.18 for 2026 (pre-rebuttal scores, new scale). The repository's own values are in results/iclr_variance.csv (column icc1_all_reviewed).

check.note: ICC values confirmed; the SD ranges hold for 2017-2019 only.
